tasks.context: Create the three Phase 4 workspace packages exactly as described by .metis/strategies/NULL/initiatives/RIT-I-0005/initiative.md: `packages/policy` exposing `resume_kit_policy`, `packages/evidence` exposing `resume_kit_evidence`, and `packages/alignment` exposing `resume_kit_alignment`. Use `packages/matching/pyproject.toml`, `packages/ats/pyproject.toml`, their `src/<pkg>/py.typed` layout, and their package-local `tests/` convention as the style reference. These packages are Python 3.12 `uv` workspace members via the existing `members = ["packages/*"]`; do not create package-local `tests/__init__.py` files because hyphenated package dirs use importlib test mode.
acceptance_criteria: All three package directories have minimal `pyproject.toml`, `README.md`, `src/<import_name>/__init__.py`, and `src/<import_name>/py.typed` files.

`resume-kit-policy` depends on `pydantic>=2`, `resume-kit-core`, and `resume-kit-schemas`; `resume-kit-evidence` depends on `pydantic>=2`, `resume-kit-core`, and `resume-kit-schemas`; `resume-kit-alignment` depends on `pydantic>=2`, `resume-kit-core`, `resume-kit-schemas`, `resume-kit-policy`, `resume-kit-evidence`, `resume-kit-matching`, and `resume-kit-ats`.
Each package uses `[tool.uv.sources]` workspace dependencies matching the existing package style.

`uv sync --all-packages` can resolve the new workspace members.

tasks.title: Add Phase 4 Result Schemas
tasks.context: Add the minimal missing Phase 4 result models required by RIT-I-0005 without duplicating existing schema substrate. Existing models to reuse are `packages/schemas/src/resume_kit_schemas/change.py` (`ChangeProposal`, `Diff`, `ResumeDiffSummary`, `ChangeSet`), `evidence.py` (`CandidateEvidence`, `EvidenceKind`), `provenance.py` (`ClaimProvenance`, `ProvenanceStatus`), plus `resume.py`, `job.py`, and `analysis.py`. The initiative calls for central models for policy decisions, alignment result envelopes, truth reports, review sessions/decisions, and skill-target plans.
acceptance_criteria: A single new schema module defines `PolicyDecision`, `PolicyRejection`, `AlignmentResult`, `TruthReport`, `ReviewSession`, `ReviewDecision`, and `SkillTargetPlan` or equivalently named minimal models covering the same concepts.

The new models compose existing `ChangeProposal`, `ChangeSet`, `Diff`, `ResumeDiffSummary`, `CandidateEvidence`, `ClaimProvenance`, `ProvenanceStatus`, `Warning`, `ATSScore`, `JobMatchReport` or `ScoreDelta` types instead of redefining them.
`PolicyDecision` records freedom level, allow/block status, reason code, human-readable explanation, and the relevant path/action.
`TruthReport` records per-claim provenance plus a deterministic pass/fail summary that can identify unsupported or contradicted claims.

`AlignmentResult` can carry original resume, aligned resume, applied/rejected changes, warnings, unresolved questions, before/after match or ATS results, truth report, and review state without requiring any CLI/API transport model.
Schema tests cover validation defaults, status/reason literals or enums, and serialization round-trips.
No existing schema files are edited except the new test file and new model module; public exports are deferred to the late export task.
tasks.implementation_notes: Place all new result types in `packages/schemas/src/resume_kit_schemas/results.py` to avoid collisions with existing `change.py`, `evidence.py`, and `provenance.py`. Use Pydantic v2 and the style from existing schema modules. Keep aliases and field names transport-agnostic. Do not add package exports here; `packages/schemas/src/resume_kit_schemas/__init__.py` is reserved for the late export task.

tasks.title: Implement Freedom Path Policy
tasks.context: Implement the deterministic policy subsystem that splits upstream `upstream/apps/backend/app/services/improver.py` path gates out of the mega-module and generalizes them for freedom 0-10. Grounding symbols are `_ALLOWED_PATH_PATTERNS` at `improver.py:80`, `_BLOCKED_PATH_PREFIXES` at `improver.py:94`, `_BLOCKED_FIELD_NAMES` at `improver.py:101`, `_is_path_allowed` at `improver.py:118`, `_is_path_blocked` at `improver.py:123`, `_sanitize_user_input` at `improver.py:48`, `_INJECTION_PATTERNS` at `improver.py:29`, and truthfulness rules from `upstream/apps/backend/app/prompts/templates.py` (`CRITICAL_TRUTHFULNESS_RULES_TEMPLATE`, `CRITICAL_TRUTHFULNESS_RULES`). Requirements REQ-402 and NFR-402 apply: no LLM, no `app.*`, factual fields blocked at every freedom level.
acceptance_criteria: Characterization tests first reproduce upstream allowed-path and blocked-path behavior at the configured upstream-equivalent freedom level.
`evaluate_change_policy(change, freedom)` or equivalent returns a schema `PolicyDecision` for a `ChangeProposal`, including allow/block, reason, path, action, and freedom level.

Freedom levels 0-10 are represented by an explicit policy table; lower levels allow narrow edits such as skills-only correction and higher levels allow broader truthful summary/description/cert/language/award edits.
Factual identity fields are blocked at every freedom level, including employer/company, title/role, dates/years, name, degree, institution, location, URLs, IDs, and metrics.
Education description remains the only editable education path; other education identity fields remain blocked as in upstream `_is_path_blocked`.
Prompt-injection sanitizer behavior is ported and tested for the upstream patterns.
Truthfulness-rule constants are exposed as deterministic strings or mappings for prompts/orchestration, with no provider dependency.
Every ported source file has the modified-source marker required by `references/attribution.md` using SHA `116f9cc3b00e1ac91734a6c2679bf41ea64a0edc`.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use `packages/policy/src/resume_kit_policy/path_policy.py` for path regexes, blocked fields, freedom table, and `PolicyDecision` construction. Use `sanitizer.py` for `_sanitize_user_input` and injection patterns. Use `truthfulness.py` for truthfulness constants adapted from upstream prompts. Keep helpers private unless needed by alignment. The task may define local reason-code constants, but schema result types live in `resume_kit_schemas.results`. Do not edit `resume_kit_policy/__init__.py`; exports are late.

tasks.title: Implement Verified Skill Targets
tasks.context: Implement the deterministic verified-skill-target gate from upstream `upstream/apps/backend/app/services/improver.py`. Grounding symbols are `_normalize_skill_key`, `_extract_skill_index`, `_skill_mentioned_in_text`, `_build_allowed_skill_target_keys`, `_extract_jd_skill_index`, `_skill_present_in_resume_text`, and `verify_skill_target_plan` around `improver.py:709` and `improver.py:754`. The RIT-I-0005 invariant is that skill additions are allowed only when already present, explicit verified-JD targets, or evidence-backed; unsupported and duplicate skills must be rejected before any diff can apply.
acceptance_criteria: Characterization tests first reproduce upstream `verify_skill_target_plan` behavior for existing skills, JD-required/preferred skills, resume-text-supported skills, unsupported skills, duplicates, malformed target lists, and punctuated skills such as `C++` and `C#`.

A public deterministic verifier accepts raw planner output, original resume data, job keywords/job description, and optional candidate evidence, returning a schema `SkillTargetPlan` with accepted and rejected targets.
Accepted targets record normalized skill, display skill, source (`existing`, `jd_added`, `supported_by_resume`, or `evidence_backed`), and reason.
Rejected targets record normalized skill, display skill, source or rejection reason, and reason text.
Duplicate skills are collapsed case-insensitively and unsupported skills are rejected.
A helper equivalent to upstream `_build_allowed_skill_target_keys` is available for the alignment apply engine without importing from alignment.
No LLM or provider imports exist in this package.
Every ported source file has the modified-source marker required by `references/attribution.md` using SHA `116f9cc3b00e1ac91734a6c2679bf41ea64a0edc`.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use `packages/policy/src/resume_kit_policy/skill_targets.py`. Keep skill normalization local to this file to avoid creating a shared utility file that would collide with the freedom-policy task. Accept plain dict resume/job shapes and canonical schema objects where straightforward. Evidence support should check `CandidateEvidence.tags` and text content conservatively; if ambiguous, reject rather than infer. Do not edit package `__init__.py`.

tasks.title: Build Candidate Evidence Truth Validation
tasks.context: Implement the new deterministic evidence engine required by REQ-406: `build_candidate_evidence(...)` and `validate_resume_truth(resume, evidence)`. Use the existing schema substrate in `packages/schemas/src/resume_kit_schemas/evidence.py` (`CandidateEvidence`, `EvidenceKind`) and `provenance.py` (`ClaimProvenance`, `ProvenanceStatus`). The truth engine should compose the structural predicates and fabrication checks from the evidence package, and it must classify material claims across the seven statuses: verified, supported, partially-supported, user-confirmed, ambiguous, unsupported, and contradicted.
acceptance_criteria: `build_candidate_evidence` extracts candidate evidence records from summary, work experience, projects, education, skills, certifications, and optional approved-claim inputs without inventing content.
Evidence IDs are stable for deterministic inputs and provenance can refer back to them.
`validate_resume_truth` returns a schema `TruthReport` containing `ClaimProvenance` records for material claims and a summary indicating whether unsupported or contradicted claims exist.
Tests cover all seven `ProvenanceStatus` values with deterministic fixtures.
Structural predicate failures and fabrication violations produce unsupported or contradicted provenance records as appropriate.
User-confirmed approved claims can support claims without adding persistence or storage.
No LLM, network, concrete provider, `app.*`, or alignment imports exist in this package.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use `packages/evidence/src/resume_kit_evidence/builder.py` for evidence construction and `truth.py` for provenance classification. Keep matching conservative: exact/casefold text matches can be `VERIFIED` or `SUPPORTED`, explicit user-confirmed evidence can be `USER_CONFIRMED`, partial token overlap can be `PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED`, no match is `UNSUPPORTED`, and structural contradiction/fabrication is `CONTRADICTED`. Do not build a database or approved-claim store; approved claims are function inputs. Do not edit package `__init__.py`.
depends_on: Port Evidence Predicates And Fabrication Checks

Grounding symbols are `apply_diffs` at `improver.py:226`, `_resolve_path`, `_set_at_path`, `_verify_original_matches` at `improver.py:215`, malformed/unsupported rejection branches at `improver.py:289-408`, reorder salvage and omitted-content preservation at `improver.py:335-363`, and skill-addition gates using `_build_allowed_skill_target_keys`. Characterization tests must come before freedom-aware generalization, using `upstream/apps/backend/tests/unit/test_apply_diffs.py` as the source of expected behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Characterization tests first cover upstream replace, append, reorder, `add_skill`, path-found, original-match, case-insensitive original match, malformed action/value rejection, duplicate skill rejection, unverified skill rejection, and reorder salvage behavior.
`apply_diffs` accepts original resume data plus a `ChangeSet` or list of `ChangeProposal`s and returns the result resume, applied changes, rejected changes, and policy/application rejection details.
Every proposed change passes through `resume_kit_policy.path_policy` and `resume_kit_policy.skill_targets` gates before mutation.

The engine deep-copies the original and does not mutate caller input.

tasks.title: Implement Review Controller
tasks.context: Implement the Phase 4 human-in-the-loop review controller as a pure state machine, not a CLI/MCP/API loop. RIT-I-0005 REQ-408 requires section-by-section review that exposes current and proposed content, change explanation, evidence for material claims, expected score impact, and decision options: approve, reject, edit, retry, reduce-freedom, increase-freedom, and skip. It must return `InterfaceResponse` with `requires_human_input` and questions using `packages/core/src/resume_kit_core/response.py` (`InterfaceResponse`, `Question`) and schema `ReviewSession` / `ReviewDecision`.
acceptance_criteria: A review session can be initialized from proposed changes, evidence/provenance, and optional score impact without applying unresolved sections.
The controller returns `InterfaceResponse.needs_input(...)` or equivalent with `requires_human_input=True` and section-specific questions when the current section is unresolved.
Approve/reject/edit/retry/reduce-freedom/increase-freedom/skip decisions update session state deterministically.
The controller does not advance past a section until that section has a terminal decision or an explicit retry/freedom-change action that reopens the same section.
Non-human-in-loop mode can produce a resolved session or bypass marker that the orchestrator can include in `AlignmentResult`.
Tests cover initialization, blocking on unresolved section, each decision action, no accidental advancement, and serialization of review state.
No CLI input, terminal prompts, MCP tool calls, provider calls, or network calls exist in this module.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use `packages/alignment/src/resume_kit_alignment/review.py`. Keep it interface-agnostic: the only transport-facing type should be `InterfaceResponse` and `Question` from core. Do not call generation or apply from this module. It should be reusable by `align_resume` but remain file-disjoint. Do not edit package `__init__.py`.

tasks.title: Implement Align Resume Orchestration
tasks.context: Implement the top-level Phase 4 engine `align_resume(...)` required by REQ-407. It wires provider proposal generation from `generation.py` to policy gating, `apply_diffs`, `verify_diff_result`, `calculate_resume_diff`, evidence truth validation, human review state, and before/after scoring through existing `packages/matching` and `packages/ats`. The critical invariant from RIT-I-0005 is that the LLM never directly writes the final document: provider output is proposal-only and must pass policy, application/verification, and truth validation before appearing in an output resume.
acceptance_criteria: `align_resume(resume, job, evidence, freedom, human_in_loop, provider)` or an equivalent typed API returns a schema `AlignmentResult`.
The pipeline order is generation/provider proposal -> policy gate -> apply -> structural verify -> structured diff -> truth validation -> score/ATS impact -> optional review response/result.
When `freedom >= 3`, truth validation always runs even if the caller did not explicitly request it.
No aligned output contains a claim with `ProvenanceStatus.UNSUPPORTED` or `ProvenanceStatus.CONTRADICTED`; such changes are rejected, stripped, or force unresolved human review.
An explicit NFR-405 adversarial test uses `FakeStructuredCompletionProvider` to propose a fabricated factual edit or unsupported claim and proves it never reaches the output resume.

Invariant tests cover blocked factual field edits at freedom 10, F>=3 auto truth validation, no unsupported/contradicted claim emission, malformed provider output, no-provider deterministic empty-change path, and human-in-loop requiring input before advancement.
Before/after score impact uses existing deterministic APIs from `resume_kit_matching` and `resume_kit_ats` without introducing cycles.
No concrete provider, network, or `app.*` import exists in alignment.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use `packages/alignment/src/resume_kit_alignment/orchestrator.py`. Keep orchestration thin and explicit rather than burying policy/evidence behavior here. If truth validation rejects a change, rerun diff/verification against the stripped result so `AlignmentResult` is internally consistent. For human-in-loop, return or embed the `InterfaceResponse`/review session rather than running an interactive loop; Phase 5 owns CLI/MCP/API wrappers.
